blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 2

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14–26, which are based on Reading Passage 2 below.

The impact of invasive species

A Invasive species are among the leading threats to the native wildlife of most countries, with approximately 42 percent of endangered species at risk from them. Invasive species can be any kind of organism – for example, a mammal, amphibian, fish, insect or plant – that is not native to an ecosystem. Often they reproduce and spread with great speed. Contrary to popular belief, a plant or animal classified as an invasive species does not necessarily originate in another country. For example, lake trout are native to the Great Lakes of North America, but are considered to be an invasive species in Yellowstone Lake in Wyoming because they compete with native cutthroat trout for habitat.

B When a new species is introduced into an ecosystem, native wildlife may struggle to compete with it for food and other resources. Invasive species can change the food web in an ecosystem by destroying or replacing native food sources, while providing little or no food for local wildlife. In extreme cases, the invader may prey on the native species. Above all, invasive species threaten biodiversity in many habitats. For instance, the climbing plant species kudzu (which is native to East Asia) can easily replace a habitat that had a wide range of plants with a monoculture consisting solely of kudzu, as has started to happen in the south-east of the USA.

C The phenomenon is not an exclusively modern one. Humans have always transferred a variety of species from one region to another, but the development of rapid means of transportation has increased the frequency of such introductions. Aquatic organisms can be shipped across the oceans, while insects can easily get into the wooden crates that are transported around the world in this way. In addition, climate change has enabled some invasive plant species to colonise new areas. Other invasive species include pets such as snakes or turtles which are intentionally set free into the wild.

D Invasive species do not all present the same level of threat to native ecosystems and can be classified into three types. The first of these may be introduced species which can maintain themselves in a limited range of habitats without upsetting the ecological equilibrium of the area. Some scientists have even argued that in these cases the introduction enhances the diversity of animal and plant life in that specific area. A second group of invaders present a greater threat because their spread is at the expense of one native species. The North American grey squirrel, for example, was introduced to the UK in 1876 largely because wealthy landowners thought it would be a fashionable and attractive addition to the local wildlife on their estates. It spread widely, leading directly to the dramatic decline in the population of the native red squirrel. However, it would appear that this is the only definite negative impact of the grey squirrel.

E There is a third level of threat in which the dominance of the introduced species has an extremely destructive effect on the entire ecosystem. One of the most damaging examples involved a species of comb jellyfish. Native to estuaries along the western Atlantic coast from the northern United States to the Valdés Peninsula in Argentina, this species was released from a ship into the Black Sea in Eastern Europe in 1982, almost certainly by accident. The Black Sea has levels of industrial waste which are by international standards exceptionally high. Despite this, fishing boats were still able to catch healthy numbers of fish. But when the invading jellyfish underwent a population explosion in the space of just six years, the entire marine ecosystem was transformed, and fish numbers declined dramatically because they were in competition with the jellyfish, preying on exactly the same microscopic creatures. The jellyfish had a more serious impact on the ecosystem than the heavily polluted water.

F More than a century after its introduction outside its native range on the Amazon River in South America, a plant known as a water hyacinth can be found in tropical lakes, streams, and rivers around the world. Its beauty attracted botanists seeking exotic plants for botanical gardens and they imported it to a horticultural exhibition in New Orleans in 1884. Visitors were so impressed they planted it in many locations during the 1880s and 1890s, resulting in the aquatic ecosystems of the south-eastern United States being progressively colonised by vast, floating, dense carpets of water hyacinth. Today it is present around the globe, damaging boat engines and even blocking cooling pipes for power plants, occasionally leading to massive blackouts. The impact of the water hyacinth on native water plants is largely unstudied, as is unfortunately the case for most ecosystems invaded by new plant species.

G In the United States, more than 7,000 introduced species have established themselves, of which at least 15 percent cause ecological damage. As the number of invasive species expands, legislation to deal with this problem is rare or non-existent in the majority of countries. Unfortunately, ordinary people outside the scientific community have a very limited understanding of the threat posed by invasive species, which means that other environmental threats receive considerably more media attention. The introduction of new species can initially seem highly desirable, but the full extent of their impact is consistently underestimated.

H Although ultimately measures need to be taken at an international level, limited action is possible by individuals. One way is for people to plant native plants in their gardens rather than species from abroad. It is also useful to learn to identify invasive species, and report any sightings to wildlife organisations. Regularly cleaning clothing, boots, boats, tyres, and any other equipment regularly used outdoors can remove insects and plant parts that may introduce invasive species into new locations.

questionGroups.bodyHtml:
Questions 14–19

Reading Passage 2 has eight paragraphs, A–H.

Which paragraph contains the following information?

Write the correct letter, A–H, in boxes 14–19 on your answer sheet.

ABCDEFGH
14 a suggestion that people have moved numerous species across the globe throughout history
15 an example of how an ecosystem can be damaged very rapidly
16 a description of what can be done to restrict the spread of invasive species
17 a reference to the lack of research on the effects of some invasive species
18 a mention of a current lack of public awareness of the problem of invasive species
19 an indication that an introduced species may benefit a specific ecosystem

Questions 20-21

Choose TWO letters, A–E.

Which TWO reasons for the spread of invasive species are mentioned in the text?

Questions 22-23

Choose TWO letters, A–E.

Which TWO statements does the writer make about the water hyacinth?

Questions 24–26

Complete the sentences below.

Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

24 Kudzu has reduced the of certain areas in the south-east of the USA.

25 Some introduced species present a low level of threat if they remain within a small area and do not disturb the of the surrounding ecosystem.

26 The effect of invasive jellyfish in the Black Sea was greater than that from factories.

passageNotes.label: Paragraph A
passageNotes.text: 入侵物种是多数国家原生野生动物的主要威胁之一，约 42% 的濒危物种受其影响。入侵物种可指任何非本地生态系统的生物（哺乳动物、两栖动物、鱼类、昆虫、植物等），通常繁殖传播迅速。与普遍认知不同，入侵物种未必来自国外 —— 例如，湖鳟原产于北美五大湖，却因与原生割喉鳟争夺栖息地，被视为怀俄明州黄石湖的入侵物种。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph B
passageNotes.text: 新物种进入生态系统后，原生生物可能难以与其争夺食物和资源；入侵物种还可能破坏或替代原生食物来源，改变食物网，甚至捕食原生物种，严重威胁生物多样性。例如，原产东亚的葛藤（kudzu）能将多样植物栖息地变为单一葛藤群落，这种情况已开始在美国东南部出现。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph C
passageNotes.text: 入侵物种并非现代独有现象 —— 人类历史上一直跨区域迁移物种，但快速交通的发展增加了迁移频率（如海洋生物随船舶传播、昆虫藏于木箱扩散）；气候变化使部分入侵植物得以扩张栖息地；此外，蛇、龟等宠物被故意放生野外，也成为入侵物种来源。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph D
passageNotes.text: 入侵物种对原生生态系统的威胁程度不同，可分为三类：第一类可在有限栖息地存活且不破坏生态平衡，部分科学家认为这类引入能增加区域生物多样性；第二类威胁更大，其扩张会导致某一原生物种减少 ——1876 年北美灰松鼠被引入英国后，导致原生红松鼠数量骤降，但灰松鼠的负面影响仅此一项；第三类威胁最大，会对整个生态系统造成毁灭性破坏。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph E
passageNotes.text: 第三类入侵物种的典型案例是一种栉水母：原产于大西洋西海岸（美国北部至阿根廷瓦尔德斯半岛），1982 年可能因意外从船舶释放进入东欧黑海。尽管黑海工业废水污染严重，但此前仍有可观渔获；然而，该水母在六年内数量暴增，与鱼类争夺微小动物，导致鱼类数量骤降，其对生态系统的破坏远超污染水体。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph F
passageNotes.text: 原产南美亚马逊河的水葫芦（water hyacinth），在引入原生范围外一个多世纪后，如今遍布全球热带湖泊、溪流和河流。1884 年，其观赏性吸引植物学家引入美国新奥尔良园艺展，19 世纪 80-90 年代游客广泛种植，导致美国东南部水生生态系统被密集漂浮的水葫芦覆盖。如今，水葫芦已全球分布，损坏船只引擎、堵塞发电厂冷却管道，偶尔引发大规模停电。遗憾的是，与多数入侵植物一样，其对原生水生植物的影响尚未得到充分研究。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph G
passageNotes.text: 美国已建立种群的引入物种超 7000 种，至少 15% 造成生态破坏。随着入侵物种增多，多数国家相关立法缺失或不完善；更严重的是，科学界外的公众对其威胁认知有限，导致其他环境问题获得更多媒体关注 —— 新物种引入初期看似有益，但人们始终低估其实际影响。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph H
passageNotes.text: 尽管最终需国际层面采取措施，个人也可采取有限行动：种植原生植物而非外来物种、学习识别入侵物种并向野生动物组织报告、定期清洁户外装备（衣物、靴子、船只、轮胎等）以清除可能携带的入侵物种。

questionExplanations.sectionTitle: 1. 段落匹配（Questions 14–19：Which paragraph contains the following information?）

items.text:
（1）题目 14：a suggestion that people have moved numerous species across the globe throughout history（提及人类历史上不断在全球迁移物种）
答案：C
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “Humans have always transferred a variety of species from one region to another”，明确提到 “人类历史上一直迁移物种”，与题干对应，因此答案为 C。

（2）题目 15：an example of how an ecosystem can be damaged very rapidly（生态系统快速受损的例子）
答案：E
解析：定位 Paragraph E 中 “when the invading jellyfish underwent a population explosion in the space of just six years, the entire marine ecosystem was transformed”，明确提到 “六年内生态系统剧变”，与题干对应，因此答案为 E。

（3）题目 16：a description of what can be done to restrict the spread of invasive species（限制入侵物种扩散的措施描述）
答案：H
解析：定位 Paragraph H 中 “plant native plants... learn to identify invasive species... regularly cleaning clothing, boots, boats...”，详细列举个人可采取的限制措施，与题干对应，因此答案为 H。

（4）题目 17：a reference to the lack of research on the effects of some invasive species（提及对部分入侵物种影响的研究缺失）
答案：F
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “The impact of the water hyacinth on native water plants is largely unstudied, as is unfortunately the case for most ecosystems invaded by new plant species”，明确提到 “水葫芦影响研究缺失”，与题干对应，因此答案为 F。

（5）题目 18：a mention of a current lack of public awareness of the problem of invasive species（提及当前公众对入侵物种问题的认知不足）
答案：G
解析：定位 Paragraph G 中 “ordinary people outside the scientific community have a very limited understanding of the threat posed by invasive species”，明确提到 “公众认知有限”，与题干对应，因此答案为 G。

（6）题目 19：an indication that an introduced species may benefit a specific ecosystem（提及引入物种可能对特定生态系统有益）
答案：D
解析：定位 Paragraph D 中 “Some scientists have even argued that in these cases the introduction enhances the diversity of animal and plant life in that specific area”，明确提到 “部分引入物种增加区域生物多样性”，与题干对应，因此答案为 D。

题目：Which TWO reasons for the spread of invasive species are mentioned in the text?（文中提及的入侵物种扩散的两个原因）
答案：D、E
选项 D：the deliberate release of non-native animals（故意放生外来动物）
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “pets such as snakes or turtles which are intentionally set free into the wild”，明确提到 “故意放生宠物”，D 正确。
- 选项 E：an extension of their geographical range as a result of global warming（全球变暖导致地理分布范围扩张）
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “climate change has enabled some invasive plant species to colonise new areas”，明确提到 “气候变化（全球变暖）使植物扩张栖息地”，E 正确。

题目：Which TWO statements does the writer make about the water hyacinth?（作者关于水葫芦的哪两项表述正确）
答案：B、D
选项 B：It was brought to North America in the late nineteenth century.（19 世纪末被引入北美）
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “imported it to a horticultural exhibition in New Orleans in 1884... planted it in many locations during the 1880s and 1890s”，明确提到 “19 世纪末引入美国（北美）”，B 正确。
- 选项 D：Its spread has caused some practical problems in recent years.（近年来其扩散引发实际问题）
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “damaging boat engines and even blocking cooling pipes for power plants, occasionally leading to massive blackouts”，明确提到 “损坏引擎、引发停电等实际问题”，D 正确。
- 排除 A：水葫芦原产亚马逊河，A 错误；排除 C：文中未提及 “因观赏性忽视负面影响”；排除 E：文中未提及 “科学家推荐引入美国”。

items.text:
（1）题目 24：Kudzu has reduced the \___\___ of certain areas in the south-east of the USA.
题目翻译：葛藤降低了美国东南部部分地区的_\___\__。
答案：biodiversity（生物多样性）
解析：定位 Paragraph B 中 “invasive species threaten biodiversity... kudzu... replace a habitat that had a wide range of plants with a monoculture”，明确提到葛藤导致 “生物多样性降低”，因此答案为 “biodiversity”。

（2）题目 25：Some introduced species present a low level of threat if they remain within a small area and do not disturb the \___\___ of the surrounding ecosystem.
题目翻译：部分引入物种若局限在小范围且不破坏周边生态系统的_\___\__，威胁程度较低。
答案：equilibrium（平衡）
解析：定位 Paragraph D 中 “without upsetting the ecological equilibrium of the area”，明确提到 “不破坏生态平衡”，因此答案为 “equilibrium”。

（3）题目 26：The effect of invasive jellyfish in the Black Sea was greater than that \___\___ from factories.
题目翻译：黑海入侵水母的影响比工厂排放的_\___\__更大。
答案：waste（废物）
解析：定位 Paragraph E 中 “The Black Sea has levels of industrial waste... The jellyfish had a more serious impact... than the heavily polluted water”，明确提到 “工业废物”，因此答案为 “waste”。
